Expected effect of this change:

- `/skills` now has a runtime enable/disable path in the TUI, mirroring the MCP toggle flow.
- Skill status is fetched from the server and reflected in the TUI, so disabled skills stay disabled across refreshes.
- The generated SDK now exposes `client.skill.status`, `client.skill.enable`, and `client.skill.disable`, which the TUI uses directly.

## Relationship to existing issues

Thank you for the pointer — this is indeed related but **distinct** from the existing issues:

- **#25137** focuses specifically on HTTP 404 "Session not found" responses. My issue covers that case **plus** the more common real-world scenario where the error never reaches the server at all (TCP socket-level failure / dead keep-alive connection). In practice, after a server restart or laptop suspend, the SDK's reqwest connection pool has a stale connection that fails at the transport layer before any HTTP request is sent.

- **#17099**, **#23997**, **#23556** describe the symptom (tools permanently lost) from different trigger angles but none propose a concrete fix.

## Key distinction: two failure modes

| Failure mode | Request reaches server? | Current behavior | Fix location |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stale session ID (404) | ✅ Yes | SDK throws, no retry | Could be server-side (strip header) OR client-side (reconnect) |
| Dead TCP connection (socket error) | ❌ No | SDK throws at transport level, no retry | **Must be client-side** |

After investigating the `@modelcontextprotocol/sdk` source and OpenCode's `convertMcpTool` in detail, the fix belongs in OpenCode's `tools()` function — wrapping `convertMcpTool` with transport-aware retry logic that leverages the existing `connect()` → `createAndStore()` path.

Happy to submit a PR if maintainers agree on the approach.

The cross-session repro is the key new fact. You exited the session with `exit`, restarted with `opencode -s ses_...`, and the cut-off persists at the same spot. That moves the diagnosis up the stack.

Two possibilities to split:

1. **Storage is incomplete** — the streaming pipeline drops content before persisting, so the session JSON doesn't have the missing text. Re-render shows the same cut-off because that's all storage has.
2. **Storage is complete, renderer cuts off deterministically** — the markdown parser hits a state issue at the same spot on the same input every time.

Quick way to tell which:

```
ls -1t ~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/info/ | head -5
# pick the recent ses_xxx, then:
cat ~/.local/share/opencode/storage/session/message/<ses_id>/*.json | jq '.parts[] | select(.type=="text") | .text' | tail -100
```

If the raw text in storage ends at "Catalog::search(&self, query: &str" — bug is in the stream→storage pipeline.
If the raw text contains the full plan but the TUI still cuts off — bug is in MarkdownRenderable's parser/render path on a deterministic input.

The build-mode evidence is independently useful. Both samples cut off at fenced-code-block boundaries: end of `</parameter></invoke>` blocks. If the storage view shows those blocks complete but the TUI doesn't, the cut-off site narrows to MarkdownRenderable's handling of code-fence close + nested `<` characters interacting with tree-sitter's HTML-inline disambiguation.

The MiniMax model is also a tell. Different providers stream chunk boundaries differently — if a stream chunk happens to split right at `</param` mid-tag, the parser's incremental state may not recover when the next chunk supplies `eter>`. Worth knowing whether the same plan rendered with Claude or GPT cuts off at the same spot or doesn't cut off at all.
